title: = NULL never matches; NULL = NULL is NULL
why: Comparison with NULL yields UNKNOWN, filtered out by WHERE, so rows vanish silently.
detect_static: Pattern: /=[[:space:]]*NULL|<>[[:space:]]*NULL/ in predicates (AST: null literal inside comparison).
detect_test: Property test: count(col = NULL) must be 0 for every column; count IS NULL + IS NOT NULL = count(*).
evidence: repro/outputs/001-null-equality.txt :: WRONG  WHERE note = NULL            -> [] (0 rows; NULL never equal)

title: NOT IN with NULL in the subquery returns nothing
why: x NOT IN (…,NULL) is UNKNOWN once one comparison is NULL, so every row is filtered out.
detect_static: NOT IN node whose subquery columns are nullable; suggest LEFT ANTI JOIN.
detect_test: Differential test: NOT IN vs LEFT ANTI JOIN on generated data with 0..30% NULL rate in the right side.
evidence: repro/outputs/002-not-in-null.txt :: WRONG  NOT IN over subquery containing NULL -> [] (0 rows)

title: Join keys with NULLs are silently dropped (=) but kept with <=>
why: Join equality is SQL =, which is UNKNOWN for NULL keys; rows with NULL keys disappear from inner joins.
detect_static: Join on nullable key without <=>; warn when null rate > 0.
detect_test: Feed rows with NULL keys, assert join output row count matches expectation (or IS NULL check appears in plan).
evidence: repro/outputs/003-join-null-keys.txt :: WRONG  equi-join ON a.k = b.k  -> [('a', 'x')] (NULL keys never match)

title: Duplicate join keys fan out rows and inflate aggregates
why: SQL join is a multiset product per matching key; duplicate keys on either side multiply rows before aggregation.
detect_static: Check uniqueness of declared key/dimension columns; join on key with duplicate values in both inputs.
detect_test: Invariant: count(join output) <= count(left)*count(right) and per-key count = l*d; assert dimension key count distinct = count.
evidence: repro/outputs/004-join-fanout.txt :: WRONG  join dup dimension keys, SUM -> [(60,)] (double counted)

title: WHERE on the right side of a LEFT JOIN kills unmatched rows
why: WHERE runs after the join; a null-rejecting predicate on the right table removes the NULL-extended rows.
detect_static: Outer join + WHERE on inner-side columns (null-rejecting predicate). Plan shows Join converted to Inner.
detect_test: Differential: same query with predicate in ON vs WHERE must agree; fail when WHERE drops rows.
evidence: repro/outputs/005-outer-join-where-vs-on.txt :: WRONG  LEFT JOIN + WHERE right.col -> [(1, 'OPEN')] (unmatched rows filtered: outer join became inner)

title: COUNT(col) vs COUNT(*); SUM of all-NULL is NULL
why: COUNT(col) counts non-NULL values only; SUM returns NULL when no non-NULL input exists, propagating NULL downstream.
detect_static: COUNT(<column>) where column is nullable and a row count was meant.
detect_test: Property: COUNT(col) + COUNT(*) >= COUNT(col); group with all NULLs must yield 0 after COALESCE.
evidence: repro/outputs/006-count-nulls-and-null-sum.txt :: WRONG expectations: COUNT(col) skips NULLs, SUM over all-NULL group is NULL not 0

title: LIMIT without ORDER BY returns arbitrary rows
why: Limit takes the first rows of an arbitrary partial order (partition layout), not a stable subset.
detect_static: LIMIT without top-level ORDER BY (parser-level lint).
detect_test: Determinism test: run LIMIT query twice with different repartitioning; results must be identical (they are not).
evidence: repro/outputs/007-limit-without-order.txt :: WRONG  repartition(8).limit(5)  -> [167, 90, 276, 203, 227]

title: Top-K with ties on ORDER BY picks arbitrary rows
why: ORDER BY is not a total order when keys tie; LIMIT then keeps an implementation-dependent subset.
detect_static: ORDER BY columns whose distinct count < row count for the limit window (needs stats); at minimum: ORDER BY key + LIMIT.
detect_test: Data with duplicate sort keys; assert the LIMIT result set is invariant under repartitioning.
evidence: repro/outputs/008-topk-ties-arbitrary.txt :: WRONG  ORDER BY score LIMIT 1 with ties: repartition(3) -> ['c'], repartition(7) -> ['c']

title: dropDuplicates keeps an arbitrary row per key
why: Dedup has no ORDER BY concept; any of the duplicates may survive depending on partitioning.
detect_static: dropDuplicates/distinctOn with columns that do not determine the surviving row.
detect_test: Duplicate keys with differing payloads under two repartitionings; outputs must match (they do not).
evidence: repro/outputs/009-dropduplicates-arbitrary-row.txt :: WRONG  dropDuplicates(['k']) repartition(3) -> [(1, 'new'), (2, 'only')]

title: Ordered window defaults to RANGE frame: peers share the running total
why: ORDER BY without an explicit frame implies RANGE BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW, which includes all rows tied on the sort key, not just the current row.
detect_static: Window function with ORDER BY and no frame clause, used as a running aggregate.
detect_test: Data with duplicate sort keys: running value must equal the ordered prefix sum (fails with RANGE).
evidence: repro/outputs/010-window-default-frame.txt :: WRONG (RANGE default; evt=2 peers share one total 80): [(1, 10, 10), (2, 20, 80), (2, 50, 80), (3, 5, 85)]

title: LAST_VALUE with the default frame returns the current row
why: Default frame ends at CURRENT ROW, so LAST_VALUE sees only rows up to the current one.
detect_static: Parser lint: LAST_VALUE/FIRST_VALUE with ORDER BY and no explicit frame.
detect_test: Sorted data: LAST_VALUE over the window must equal the max(evt) row value (fails by default).
evidence: repro/outputs/011-last-value-default-frame.txt :: WRONG  LAST_VALUE with default frame -> [(1, 10), (2, 20), (3, 30)] (frame ends at current row, returns current value)

title: RANK gaps after ties vs DENSE_RANK; ROW_NUMBER is arbitrary on ties
why: RANK counts peers (gap), DENSE_RANK does not; ROW_NUMBER assigns arbitrary but unique numbers to tied rows.
detect_static: Ranking function choice near pagination/top-N logic; flag RANK used for offsets.
detect_test: Fixed tie data; assert expected (rk,drk) triples as above.
evidence: repro/outputs/012-rank-vs-dense-rank.txt :: RANK leaves gaps after ties (see player c/d), DENSE_RANK does not, ROW_NUMBER invents a total order:

title: Unseeded rand() re-evaluates per action; two actions disagree
why: Nondeterministic expressions are recomputed on every action (no seed, no cache), so filters/samples are not reproducible.
detect_static: rand()/random()/uuid() without seed used in filters or joins keys.
detect_test: Run the same action twice; counts must be equal (they are not), or seed the generator.
evidence: repro/outputs/013-rand-nondeterministic.txt :: WRONG  rand() without seed: count run1 = 10033, run2 = 10113 (re-evaluated per action, differs)

title: DISTINCT dedups the whole selected row, not the first column
why: SELECT DISTINCT removes duplicate row tuples; extra selected columns re-introduce values that looked deduplicated.
detect_static: DISTINCT with more projected columns than the intended key.
detect_test: Assert output count equals count(distinct intended key).
evidence: repro/outputs/014-distinct-vs-groupby.txt :: WRONG  DISTINCT applies to the whole row: SELECT DISTINCT a,b -> [(1, 'x'), (1, 'y'), (2, 'z')] (2 kept, a=1 twice)

title: UNION deduplicates by default (semantics + hidden shuffle cost)
why: Bare UNION is UNION DISTINCT: correctness surprise when duplicates are meaningful and an avoidable shuffle+dedup cost.
detect_static: Parser lint: UNION without ALL.
detect_test: Row-count invariant: sum of input counts must equal output count when inputs are known disjoint.
evidence: repro/outputs/015-union-dedup.txt :: WRONG  UNION (implicit DISTINCT) count -> [(3,)] (3; dedup you may not want, plus a full shuffle)

title: EXCEPT drops duplicates of the left side (set vs multiset)
why: EXCEPT DISTINCT returns each surviving row once regardless of how often it occurred on the left.
detect_static: EXCEPT/MINUS/INTERSECT without ALL over tables where multiplicity matters.
detect_test: Differential: EXCEPT vs EXCEPT ALL on data with left-side duplicates.
evidence: repro/outputs/016-except-set-semantics.txt :: WRONG  EXCEPT (set semantics) -> [(1,)] (one 1; multiplicity of duplicates is lost)

title: SUM over DOUBLE depends on partitioning (float addition is not associative)
why: Partial aggregation merges in partition order; reordering floating point additions changes the result.
detect_static: SUM/AVG over DOUBLE/FLOAT columns compared for exact equality, or used as join keys.
detect_test: Differential: same data in 1 vs N partitions must give bitwise-equal sums (it does not).
evidence: repro/outputs/017-float-sum-order.txt :: WRONG/fragile  1 partition  sum -> 1.0

title: DECIMAL overflow raises; scale truncation and DOUBLE casts lose digits silently
why: DECIMAL arithmetic overflow throws ArithmeticException (Spark 4.2, quoted), but narrowing casts and DOUBLE conversions round/lose digits with no error.
detect_static: CAST between DECIMAL precisions/scales and DOUBLE on money columns.
detect_test: Property: value round-trips through the declared type (fails for 12.25 -> DECIMAL(10,1)).
evidence: repro/outputs/018-decimal-precision-loss.txt :: DECIMAL(38,0)*DECIMAL(38,0) -> ERROR [NUMERIC_VALUE_OUT_OF_RANGE.WITH_SUGGESTION]  999999999999999999999999999999999999990 cannot be represented as Decimal(38, 0). If necessary

title: HALF_UP vs HALF_EVEN rounding disagree across Spark round/bround, cast, Python
why: Spark ROUND and decimal CAST are HALF_UP; BROUND is HALF_EVEN; Python round is HALF_EVEN to even. Money rounding must be pinned explicitly.
detect_static: ROUND on money columns compared against non-Spark systems.
detect_test: Fixed .5 inputs across engines/functions; assert the chosen policy everywhere.
evidence: repro/outputs/019-decimal-rounding.txt :: Python round(2.5) = 2 (banker's rounding, HALF_EVEN by default)

title: Integer overflow: wraparound (non-ANSI int add, verified), exception (ANSI), try_add (explicit)
why: Non-ANSI int add wraps silently (INT_MAX+1 -> -2147483648, quoted in run output); ANSI mode raises so the job fails loudly. (First believed NULL from docs; corrected after running - see repro/outputs/020-integer-overflow.txt.)
detect_static: Arithmetic on INT/BIGINT columns near type limits; check spark.sql.ansi.enabled.
detect_test: Property: non-NULL inputs must produce non-NULL output (fails non-ANSI).
evidence: repro/outputs/020-integer-overflow.txt :: ansi=True bigint+1 over MAX -> ERROR [ARITHMETIC_OVERFLOW] overflow. Use 'try_add' to tolerate overflow and return NULL instead. If necessary set "spark.sql.

title: 1/0: Spark NULL (non-ANSI) or exception (ANSI); DuckDB inf; sqlite NULL
why: Division by zero is handled per engine/mode; DuckDB yields IEEE inf which propagates into averages instead of vanishing.
detect_static: Division where the divisor column can be 0; no NULLIF/try_divide guard.
detect_test: Feed divisor 0; assert policy explicitly (NULL, error, or inf) and compare engines for portability.
evidence: repro/outputs/021-division-by-zero.txt :: duckdb 1/0             -> [(inf,)] (inf, not NULL!)

title: CAST('abc' AS INT): Spark NULL, DuckDB error, sqlite 0 — silent row loss
why: Non-ANSI Spark coerces unparseable strings to NULL inside predicates, so rows disappear instead of failing; engines disagree.
detect_static: CAST(string_col AS numeric) inside WHERE/JOIN; suggest try_cast + IS NULL audit count.
detect_test: Audit query: count rows where col IS NOT NULL AND try_cast(col AS INT) IS NULL must be 0 when column is expected numeric.
evidence: repro/outputs/022-cast-string-silent-null.txt :: WRONG  WHERE CAST(s AS INT) > 5 -> [('12',)] ('abc' and NULL vanished; no error, no warning)

title: Comparing string column to number silently casts (and silently drops)
why: Type coercion casts the string side to the numeric type; unparseable values become NULL and never match, with no error.
detect_static: Binary comparison/join with mismatched string vs numeric types (AST type check).
detect_test: For key columns, assert count(col <> CAST(col AS INT)::STRING) is 0 to detect unparseable keys.
evidence: repro/outputs/023-implicit-cast-compare.txt :: implicit cast string vs int comparisons: [(True, True, None)] ('abc'=10 is UNKNOWN, not false)

title: ANSI/cast/overflow behaviour differs by version and spark.sql.ansi.enabled
why: Same statement yields NULL, an error, or a value depending on version and mode; upgrades change results silently.
detect_static: Config audit of spark.sql.ansi.enabled; try_* vs plain functions inventory.
detect_test: Run the fixed cross_queries list on both versions/modes in CI and diff (this repo does exactly that).
evidence: repro/outputs/024-ansi-mode-3-vs-4.txt :: cast_inf ansi=False OK [(inf,)]

title: Same timestamp string parses to different instants per session time zone
why: TIMESTAMP parsing uses spark.sql.session.timeZone; a job run under a different default zone reads another instant.
detect_static: to_timestamp/unix_timestamp without explicit zone; check spark.sql.session.timeZone.
detect_test: Parse one known string under two session zones; epochs must differ by the zone offset (they do).
evidence: repro/outputs/025-timezone-session-parse.txt :: session tz Europe/Warsaw   -> [(1781517600,)]

title: DST gap/overlap wall-clock times are shifted or ambiguous
why: Local timestamps without offset have no unique instant during DST transitions; Spark resolves gap times forward and picks one side on overlap.
detect_static: Timestamp literals/strings in local time around known transition dates; prefer 'yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss XXX' with offset.
detect_test: Feed 02:30 on both EU transition dates of the year; assert epoch monotonicity per hour (violated).
evidence: repro/outputs/026-timezone-dst-gap.txt :: Europe/Warsaw 2026-10-25 02:30 exists twice (DST overlap): -> [(datetime.datetime(2026, 10, 25, 2, 30), 1792888200)]

title: to_timestamp with wrong pattern returns NULL for all rows
why: Parse failures are NULLs, not exceptions, so a format mismatch empties the pipeline silently.
detect_static: Literal format vs sampled data format; regex pre-check of one value.
detect_test: Property: to_timestamp(col, fmt) IS NULL rate must be 0 on a known-good sample.
evidence: repro/outputs/027-timestamp-format-silent-null.txt :: A wrong format string yields NULL for every row (no error) in this non-ANSI session: downstream filters/joins silently drop everything.

title: Jan 31 + INTERVAL 1 MONTH clamps to Feb 28 silently
why: Month arithmetic clamps out-of-range days instead of failing or preserving the day number.
detect_static: add_months / INTERVAL n MONTH on day > 28 data.
detect_test: Dates on the 29th-31st; assert the business rule (clamped vs error vs last_day) explicitly.
evidence: repro/outputs/028-date-month-end-clamp.txt :: Spark: [(datetime.date(2026, 2, 28), datetime.date(2026, 2, 28))] (day clamped to month end, silently)

title: String ORDER BY is binary codepoint order, not locale/collation order
why: Default collation is binary (UTF8String bytes); 'Zebra' < 'apple' and accented characters sort at the end.
detect_static: ORDER BY/LIKE/MIN/MAX on user-visible text without explicit collation; Spark 4 has COLLATE.
detect_test: Fixed multilingual sample; assert the expected locale order (fails under binary).
evidence: repro/outputs/029-string-ordering-binary.txt :: sqlite 'Zebra' < 'apple': [(1,)] (1 = true; binary, same as Spark)

title: Join keys differing only in case match nothing (= is case-sensitive)
why: String equality is byte equality; data merged from systems with different casing silently loses all matches.
detect_static: JOIN on free-text/name columns without lower()/initcap normalization.
detect_test: Sample-key overlap check: count of join keys matching case-insensitively minus exactly must be ~0 if clean.
evidence: repro/outputs/030-case-sensitive-join.txt :: WRONG  join on raw name (case differs) -> [(0,)] rows (all pairs dropped)

title: CSV inferSchema turns '001' into 1: leading zeros lost, joins fail
why: Type inference picks numeric for digit-only columns; codes with leading zeros are corrupted before they reach a join.
detect_static: read.csv(inferSchema=True) on files with code-like columns; require explicit schema.
detect_test: Round-trip check: count rows where csv value <> cast-to-string of parsed value on a sample.
evidence: repro/outputs/031-csv-inferschema-leading-zeros.txt :: WRONG join of inferred csv vs string dim table -> [0] matched rows (expect 3)

title: User input inside LIKE: % and _ act as wildcards
why: Interpolating search text into a LIKE pattern lets users match unintended rows (or all rows with a bare %).
detect_static: LIKE with concatenated user input and no ESCAPE clause; string-built SQL.
detect_test: Search for '10%' and '%': result sets must contain exactly the literal rows.
evidence: repro/outputs/032-like-pattern-injection.txt :: WRONG  LIKE '%%10%%' unescaped -> [('10 percent',), ('10%',), ('1000',), ('A100',)] (wildcard % matches any suffix)

title: Missing join condition turns the query into a cartesian product
why: A WHERE clause that only filters one side leaves the join without a predicate; output and cost multiply by both row counts.
detect_static: Join node without equality condition; CROSS JOIN in plan; row-count estimate >> inputs.
detect_test: Plan assertion: no CartesianProduct node; row-count sanity check.
evidence: repro/outputs/033-cartesian-missing-join.txt :: WRONG  missing join predicate (comma join, only WHERE filter) -> 1500 rows (cartesian)

title: sortWithinPartitions is not a global ORDER BY
why: Rows are sorted inside each partition; collect/limit over the result is interleaved, not globally ordered.
detect_static: DataFrame API sortWithinPartitions followed by collect/limit/write-single-file.
detect_test: Assert monotonicity of the collected sort key (fails).
evidence: repro/outputs/034-sort-within-partitions.txt :: WRONG  repartition(4).sortWithinPartitions('k') first 8 (id,k): [(1, 1), (21, 1), (17, 1), (18, 2), (2, 2), (19, 3), (20, 0), (13, 1)] (sorted only inside partitions)

title: LIKE case sensitivity differs: sqlite insensitive, Spark/DuckDB sensitive
why: SQL standard LIKE is case-sensitive, but sqlite (and MySQL) default to insensitive ASCII matching; ports change result sets.
detect_static: LIKE predicates ported across engines; add lower() both sides or explicit COLLATE.
detect_test: Differential run of the same LIKE on both engines; result sets must match (they do not).
evidence: repro/outputs/035-like-case-sensitivity-portability.txt :: DuckDB 'Apple' LIKE 'a%' -> [(False,)] (case-sensitive)
